item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"B is substantially closer to the frozen contract and is the preferable review base, though it still needs revision before merge.","reasons":["B adds the exact Upload signature and reuses internal/multipartbody.NewFile with field \"file\", producing a replayable buffered multipart body.","B’s retry test uses an open file as streamed source and verifies field name, filename, content, and identical content across the 429 retry.","A explicitly adds forbidden association-field functionality, introduces NewFileWithFields, and changes FilesOption behavior.","A makes broad, unrelated changes to RawClient retry and reader-ownership semantics, contrary to the contract’s scope constraints and with greater regression risk than B’s localized implementation."],"risks_a":["Upload bypasses FilesService.Add and duplicates its option handling, request construction, response decoding, and missing-data checks.","Adds WithFilesFormFields and association fields despite the explicit prohibition.","Globally changes seekable-body replay, Content-Length detection, and closing semantics in RawClient; GetBody also reuses the same mutable seeker rather than returning an independent reader recreation path with narrower scope expected by the contract/tests pattern in repo (buffered helpers). Also if SeekEnd fails, the initial reader position is not explicitly restored before first send, depending on seeker behavior after failed seek, a subtle generic-reader risk. If SeekEnd succeeds, it works sequentially, but still broadens behavior and ownership semantics globally beyond requested scope. This violates contract regardless of whether tests pass. Also the changelog documents changed Raw.Do ownership semantics, confirming intentional API behavior change. Moreover Upload uses NewFileWithFields rather than directly using established NewFile as required, despite NewFile delegating to it; reviewer burden and added machinery are unnecessary. A's Upload retry test uses strings.NewReader instead of an open/streaming source and does not test source-reader errors. A does validate filename/nil before helper, but then helper also validates, a little duplication. A’s new multipart helper tests don't test source read failures either. Finally, A adds README docs for forbidden association option and unrelated generic retry semantics, increasing scope/churn. The exact risks list can mention only concise items. Need valid output. Let's rewrite JSON cleanly. "],"risks_b":["FilesService.Add now eagerly buffers every custom multipart body, changing its existing streaming and source-read error behavior despite the requirement to preserve Add behavior.","Upload calls a new private add helper instead of routing through the existing public Add method as explicitly required.","Tests omit required empty-filename, nil-content, and source-reader failure cases."]}
